Klarna Goes Global With Anti-Scam Call Verification
summary:
Klarna, the everyday finance network, today announced its popular in-app Call Status Detection tool is now live globally, giving consumers a reliable and simple way to check whether someone calling them is genuinely from Klarna.
Call Status Detection has already helped thousands of consumers verify calls since it launched in the Nordics  in September. The feature has now been rolled out globally, reflecting Klarna’s commitment to protecting its customers from fraud.
Call Status Detection is quick and easy to use by design. If a customer takes a call from someone claiming to be Klarna, all they have to do is open the Klarna app and check the banner at the top of their screen — green means the call is verified and it is safe to continue, while amber means Klarna cannot verify the call and the customer should hang up.
The feature builds on Klarna’s existing anti-fraud measures like the Klarna Inbox, which enables verification of written communication like emails, texts and letters, and aims to protect customers by making it harder for scammers to impersonate Klarna. 
“Scammers are a global problem, so our protections need to be too,” said Klarna Head of Financial Crime Woody Malouf. “Every Klarna customer now gets the same simple check. No need to hunt for a number, just open the app, look at the colour, and you know whether it’s safe to keep talking.”
Fraudsters impersonating banks and payment providers over the phone has become one of the fastest-growing threats to consumers, and caller ID can be spoofed easily. Fraudsters stole an estimated $579 billion worldwide through scams and bank fraud in 2025, according to Nasdaq Verafin.
Call Status Detection will be enabled by default in the Klarna app for iOS users in all 26 markets where Klarna operates. Android users will need to enable the feature in their Klarna app settings.

LexisNexis Risk Solutions Extends Risk Intelligence to Agentic Activity
summary:
LexisNexis® Risk Solutions has extended its powerful risk intelligence solutions to help organisations understand and assess a new class of digital actor: AI agents operating on behalf of people and businesses.
For decades, LexisNexis Risk Solutions has helped organisations make risk decisions by connecting identity, device, behavioural, network and transaction intelligence at global scale. As AI agents become another participant in digital interactions, the company is extending that same connected intelligence approach to agentic activity.
Know Your Agent (KYA) intelligence adds a new layer of agentic insights to LexisNexis Risk Solutions’ digital identity and fraud prevention platform. It helps organisations recognise when AI agents are interacting with their digital services and can bring those interactions directly into established risk assessment and decisioning workflows, rather than treating them as an isolated risk problem. Many LexisNexis Risk Solutions customers are already using KYA intelligence in their current risk management decision making.
Analysis of global digital transactions by LexisNexis Risk Solutions shows agentic traffic grew over 750% in the first half of 2026 alone. Rapid growth is expected to continue as more people and organisations adopt agents to undertake everyday tasks such as online shopping.
Because most personal agents today do not self-declare as agents, organisations face an immediate challenge: distinguishing agentic activity from other digital traffic. But this is only the first step. Agent detection alone cannot answer key questions organisations ultimately need to resolve: Who or what is the agent acting for? Has that activity been authorised? Is its behaviour consistent with that authority? And does the wider context of the interaction indicate that it is legitimate?
That context may also change during a digital journey as control passes between a person and an AI agent, making continuous visibility into the interaction increasingly important. This is where the scale and connectivity of the Risk Intelligence Network becomes essential.
AI-agent activity does not need to be evaluated as an isolated interaction. It can be understood in the context of the identities, devices, networks, behavioural patterns and relationships surrounding digital activity, helping to provide richer context for risk decisions. This connected intelligence approach incorporates agent detection into risk decisions in real time, while aiding in creating a foundation for increasingly sophisticated agent identity and authorisation capabilities as agents, standards and use cases evolve.
Autonomous AI agents have the potential to increase the scale and sophistication of fraud, including authorised push payment fraud and account takeover attacks. Malicious agents can learn dynamically from successes and failures, enabling subsequent attacks to become more tailored and prolific.
For organisations, the decision is not whether an agent is universally trusted but whether a specific agent, acting in a specific context, should be permitted to perform a specific action. Legitimate agents will increasingly participate in digital customer journeys, but the appropriate response will depend on what the agent is attempting to do, the context of the interaction, and the organisation’s own risk policies. KYA intelligence helps organisations bring agentic activity into existing decisioning workflows so they can allow, authenticate, review or reject interactions as appropriate.
“Agentic commerce is moving quickly from experimentation into the mainstream,” said Grayson Clarke, chief commercial officer at LexisNexis Risk Solutions. “Agentic transactions globally more than doubled again in the last quarter, driven primarily by personal agents. Some businesses are enabling agents to transact on consumers’ behalf, while others are restricting their activities, and many are still determining the right approach. We have already seen firsthand how a global financial institution used our detection capabilities to help identify agentic activity and prevent it from executing sensitive transactions.”
LexisNexis Risk Solutions analysed more than 116 billion digital transactions globally in 2025 through its LexisNexis® Digital Identity Network®, giving it a uniquely broad view of how human, automated and increasingly agentic interactions are evolving. The network detected 4.9 billion automated bot attacks during the year, a 59% increase year over year. That scale reflects the role LexisNexis Risk Solutions already plays in helping many of the world's largest financial institutions, merchants and digital businesses assess risk across digital interactions.
Mike Woodberry, senior vice president of product and analytics at LexisNexis Risk Solutions, added, “Managing risk in the agentic economy will require more than agent detection alone. The real challenge is establishing context: what is acting, who or what it represents, whether it is authorised and what it is attempting to do. Our vision for KYA is to extend established risk intelligence into the agentic economy, helping give organisations the flexibility to apply the appropriate response to each interaction rather than relying on a one-size-fits-all risk assessment.”
Woodberry continued, “Organisations should not have to build a new risk strategy every time digital interactions evolve. Adding a new layer of agentic insights to our established identity and fraud prevention platform helps customers build on the capabilities they already rely on while preparing for the next generation of digital interactions.”

content: LexisNexis Risk Solutions has extended its risk intelligence platform to address the growing activity of AI agents in digital transactions. The new Know Your Agent intelligence layer helps organizations recognize AI agents, assess their authorization, and integrate these insights into existing fraud prevention workflows. As agentic commerce rapidly expands, this connected approach provides critical context to manage risks without treating AI interactions as isolated problems.

title: Nexi and Deutsche Telekom Selected by the European Central Bank to Provide Digital Euro Network Service Provider (NSP) Connectivity
summary:
Nexi, in temporary grouping with Deutsche Telekom, has been selected by the European Central Bank (ECB) as one of the two successful tenderers, for the provision of Network Service Provider (NSP) Connectivity for the digital euro, and the one providing NSP services to support the pilot project. This announcement follows the conclusion of the ECB's negotiated public procurement procedure to select contractors for the provision of secure, reliable, and high-performance connectivity services for the future digital currency.
The implementation of this high-performance network—which will interconnect the data centers hosting the components of the Digital Euro Service Platform (DESP) as well as enable crucial external actors such as Payment Service Providers (PSPs) and National Central Banks to access the Digital Euro Service Platform (DESP)—is a foundational pillar for the successful launch and operation of the digital euro project.
The joint solution proposed by Nexi and Deutsche Telekom offers a robust and scalable connectivity and mediation platform designed to enable the end-to-end exchange of digital euro transactions across the entire DESP ecosystem. Engineered to guarantee the smooth delivery of digital euro services to end-users, the architecture supports high levels of scalability and elasticity, allowing resources to be adjusted efficiently to meet varying transaction volumes and peak usage scenarios.
The total duration of the service agreement is ten years from the contract's official start date.
“The ECB’s decision to award the temporary grouping Nexi and Deutsche Telekom one of the two digital euro connectivity contracts represents an important milestone for our Group and further confirms Nexi’s role as a strategic infrastructure partner in the European payments’ ecosystem. The digital euro is a key initiative for the future of payments and for strengthening Europe’s digital sovereignty” commented Bernardo Mingrone, CEO of Nexi Group. “This ten-year service agreement represents a significant industrial achievement, recognizing our technological capabilities and Nexi’s ability to make a concrete contribution to an initiative of this scale. With our pan-European scale, strong local presence and distinctive technological expertise, Nexi is positioned to help driving the digital euro transformation and the future evolution of digital payments, providing a secure, resilient and scalable infrastructure to support banks, businesses and institutions across the euro area.”
“The euro area financial ecosystem depends on secure, resilient and trusted digital infrastructure. As Europe’s largest telecommunications company, Deutsche Telekom, together with our partners, is proud to contribute to the digital euro initiative led by the ECB on behalf of the Eurosystem. For decades, we have delivered mission-critical connectivity and digital services to governments, public institutions and enterprises across Europe. Through initiatives such as European quantum communication infrastructure and IRIS² and other classified network projects with security or government institutions, Deutsche Telekom is helping build the secure, resilient digital infrastructure Europe needs to protect its institutions, strengthen its strategic autonomy and advance its digital sovereignty. This contribution reflects our long-term commitment to strengthening Europe’s digital sovereignty and supporting the resilience of its financial infrastructure (Gottfried Ludewig, Senior Vice President / Leader Public Sector and Health Industry Deutsche Telekom).”
